title: Jina AI Releases jina-ocr-v1: A 3.4B MoE Document Parser With Built-In Speculative Decoding for Low-Budget GPUs
summary: Jina AI has released jina-ocr-v1, a visual document parser that converts PDFs, scans, tables, charts and invoices into Markdown. The model has 3.4B total parameters, with about 570M active per token, and builds on DeepSeek-OCR. A built-in FastMTP speculative decoding head drafts 3 tokens per step while keeping output lossless. It scores 91.14 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and 83.4 on olmOCR-Bench, and parses 2.57 pages per second on 1 A100. Weights are on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0, with hosted access through Jina Reader. The post Jina AI Releases jina-ocr-v1: A 3.4B MoE Document Parser With Built-In Speculative Decoding for Low-Budget GPUs appeared first on MarkTechPost .
title_en: Jina AI Releases jina-ocr-v1: A 3.4B MoE Document Parser With Built-In Speculative Decoding for Low-Budget GPUs
title_zh: Jina AI 发布 jina-ocr-v1：3.4B MoE 文档解析器，内置投机解码适配低预算 GPU
summary_en: Jina AI released jina-ocr-v1, a 3.4B MoE visual document parser converting PDFs, scans, tables, charts and invoices into Markdown. Built on DeepSeek-OCR with FastMTP speculative decoding, it scores 91.14 on OmniDocBench v1.6 and parses 2.57 pages/second on one A100.
summary_zh: Jina AI 发布 jina-ocr-v1，一款 3.4B MoE 视觉文档解析器，可将 PDF、扫描件、表格、图表和发票转为 Markdown。基于 DeepSeek-OCR，内置 FastMTP 投机解码，OmniDocBench v1.6 得分 91.14，单张 A100 每秒解析 2.57 页。

title: Why Europe has been absent from the great AI safety debate
summary: Though Europe has measures that address how consumers might encounter AI, technology will impact them if the worst scenarios bear Europe’s dilemma over AI was rendered in stark terms this week. The head of the continent’s central bank, Christine Lagarde, said Europeans have two options: shun the technology and lose out on growth; or embrace it and become dependent on tools developed by the US and China. The great debate over AI safety that has erupted in recent days threatens to make the choice moot. If the worst scenarios come to bear – and experts have differing views on this – then the technology will impact the continent regardless. Continue reading...
